brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Four hex bases at level 0 (full at -1,0 / 0,0 / 0,1 and a half-w at 1,0) plus a full base at 0,0,1 stacked on top as a shelf cell. Mesh check is clear. The build is a small prototype; I did not design a full set of open shelving bays for book storage.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: This configurator checks fit and mesh clearance, not strength, and I have no load rating for the bases, joint bolts or drawer frames. I cannot claim a 50 kg rating from this build.
Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at the empty positions -1,1,0 (notch 0) and 0,-1,0 (notch 4), each bridging two bases. Both accepted and the mesh check is clear.

finish.summary: Built a small hex-base shelf unit with two notch drawer frames at level 0 and one shelf cell above. check_build reports no errors and meshClash clear. Only LOOSE_BODY warning was resolved by adding a joint bolt. The two-drawer requirement is met. The 50 kg load rating cannot be verified by this fit-only checker, so it is unmet as a claim. The shelf is a minimal prototype, not a full book-storage design.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
